Not quite yet. The game has a great premise with a lot of potential for additional content and tweaks, but it's incredibly rough right now at launch state. The game play loop is no different than any other types of simulator games: daily routine of wake up, get shipments, place accordingly, open shop, make profit, make small meta progress by leveling up to unlock new stuff or finally save enough money to buy a new part of the area, go to bed, repeat. The innovation here is a night time zombie invasion where they come to destroy your money making graves at night to which there are a few lines of defenses: barricades akin to Call of Duty zombies, then turrets / fences / floor traps, you know the deal. All of the above sounds like it's a recipe for success, but the game just doesn't quite scratch the itch for me. It constantly feels like I'm struggling to keep my head above the water with expenses and zombies breaking stuff. Normally I'd agree with "skill issue", especially since other people don't seem to have as much trouble with the combat, but it's kind of everything being too much: - I'm aware the devs are aware of NPCs "sticking" - meaning they freeze and don't do their job without a reset, however my florist needs to be reset 3 times per day minimum which causes customers to leave and I lose out on a significant amount of much needed income. - The constant need of refreshing ammo for turrets / replacing broken fences / replacing flowers (especially when Garden is the last thing you're likely to unlock) is insanely expensive for how much you need. The game time could be cut in half if the items weren't so expensive and many nights are you just waiting for the next day's income to compensate. Forget about affording upgrades too. - Four entrances for the zombies to come in feels a bit much. I think either two at the far end or one "mega" entrance would definitely make the game feel a lot better as it would allow for more strategic planning, especially since there's one entrance that gets a burst of zombies, the rest only get a few, and there's no indicator to tell you which one it is. I think this game could be a lot better if it was balanced a bit more in terms of costs and income, plus some additional content + fixing the NPCs. For $15, I would expect a lot more than what's here, especially in the state that it's in.

[h1]没有明显缺点，但也少点亮点[/h1] [h2]游戏概况[/h2] 白天墓园经营（埋尸、卖花、员工管理）+夜晚僵尸塔防的混合玩法，含黑色幽默元素，支持放松模式。 创意亮眼但内容短，前10小时新鲜，后期重复枯燥，bug较多，适合打折尝鲜。 [h2]推荐指数★★★（3/5星）[/h2] [h2]推荐理由[/h2] “经营+塔防”反差玩法独特，放松模式包容休闲玩家；开发者响应及时，首日修复关键bug；前期成长节奏舒适，6-10小时可解锁全成就。 25天后无新内容，僵尸类型单一（仅4-5种）；员工AI频繁卡墙，存档机制反人类（仅夜间自动存档）；经济后期失衡，防御过度导致夜间“看戏”。 [h2]推荐与不推荐人群[/h2] - [b]适合玩家[/b]：每天1-2小时的碎片时间休闲玩家、喜欢脑洞玩法的猎奇者、追求快速解锁成就的玩家。 - [b]不适合玩家[/b]：追求长线内容深度的玩家、联机刚需者（无合作模式）、对bug和操作缺陷容忍度低的细节控。 [hr][/hr] [h2]数据统计[/h2] - [b]推荐/不推荐占比[/b]：推荐280条（89.17%），不推荐34条（10.83%）；不推荐多因“内容短、重复度高”。 - [b]推荐玩家时长[/b]：最长60.1小时，平均9.84小时，中位数8.4小时（多数10小时内通关）。 - [b]不推荐玩家时长[/b]：最长30.4小时，平均8.82小时，中位数6.3小时（多因重复感提前退出）。 - [b]语种分布与好评率[/b]：中文102条（32.5%，94%好评）＞日文22条（7%，91%好评）＞德文18条（5.7%，89%好评）＞英文158条（50.3%，87%好评）＞其他14条（4.5%）。 [hr][/hr] [h2]15条游戏优点（按提及频率降序）[/h2] [h3]1. 玩法创新性与独特性[/h3] - [b]日经营+夜塔防的反差爽感[/b]：白天执行埋尸、卖花、员工管理等经营操作，夜晚切换第一人称塔防对抗僵尸，像《i>墓地管理员》与《i>COD僵尸模式》的结合，脑洞巧妙。 - [b]放松模式的包容性[/b]：为FPS苦手或休闲玩家屏蔽僵尸威胁，仅保留经营核心，避免挫败感（“没有放松模式早删游，终于能安心种花”）。 - [b]黑色幽默细节加分[/b]：尸体用“Ute货车”运送、荒诞死因（“被熊袭击”“极端节食”）、员工翻译梗（“train标为‘火车’，fire标为‘火’”），增强趣味性。 - [b]武器与防御策略性[/b]：枪械有Doom式慢动作切换，铁锹爆头爽感足；支持“特斯拉电塔+铁丝网围堵”等布局，策略性受认可。 - [b]经营模拟沉浸感[/b]：尸体腐烂倒计时、墓碑清洁度影响收入、员工分工明确（花商补货、技师修墙），还原“墓园老板”真实感。 - [b]低成本高创意框架[/b]：Unity引擎画面粗糙，但“经营+塔防”玩法扎实，比多数换皮模拟器更有新意。 [h3]2. 核心玩法[/h3] - [b]短平快的成长节奏[/b]：6-10小时可解锁全设施与成就，无冗长肝度，适合碎片时间（“10小时全成就，不用熬夜肝，很舒服”）。 - [b]经济系统初期挑战[/b]：前期缺钱需精打细算，贷款机制缓解压力，后期自动化实现“躺赚”，符合“从穷到富”爽感曲线。 - [b]防御布局自由度[/b]：4个僵尸入口可自定义陷阱与炮塔位置，支持“栅栏引导路线+集中火力”，灵活度高。 - [b]员工系统减负明显[/b]：雇佣后分担卖花、种地、修墙等重复工作，让玩家专注核心经营与夜间防御（“有了花商，不用天天手动补货”）。 [h3]3. 品质与沉浸感[/h3] - [b]复古画风适配主题[/b]：低模卡通风格贴合“黑色幽默”调性，夜晚僵尸潮BGM增强氛围（“PS2时代丧尸片质感，怀旧带感”）。 - [b]墓园装饰个性化[/b]：支持摆放长椅、路灯、自定义墓碑位置，满足“强迫症摆烂”需求（“把墓园修成小花园，白天看访客散步很治愈”）。 - [b]种田系统平衡节奏[/b]：种花卖钱、种菜回血的休闲玩法，与夜间高强度塔防形成动静平衡（“白天浇花解压，晚上打僵尸发泄，节奏刚好”）。 [h3]4. 基础体验[/h3] - [b]运行优化及格[/b]：多数设备（含Steam Deck）可稳定运行，中低画质无明显卡顿（“Steam Deck开低画质45帧，不影响操作”）。 - [b]开发者响应及时[/b]：首日修复员工卡住、存档丢失等bug，公布更新roadmap，玩家认可“反馈后当天热修，诚意比大厂足”。 [hr][/hr] [h2]15条玩家不满意的问题（按提及频率降序）[/h2] [h3]1. 重复可玩性[/h3] - [b]内容量短，后期极度枯燥[/b]：25天后无新设施、新僵尸，每日重复“经营+防守”，像“打卡上班”（“解锁所有炮塔后，每天只是补弹药、收尸体”）。 - [b]僵尸类型单一无新意[/b]：仅4-5种基础僵尸，无BOSS战或特殊敌人，后期全为换皮怪（“第30天僵尸和第5天一样，无挑战性”）。 - [b]经济后期严重失衡[/b]：自动化后资金过剩，防御过度导致僵尸“刚进门就被秒”，玩家沦为“旁观者”（“钱花不完，僵尸打不着，后期像看PPT”）。 - [b]墓园扩展受限[/b]：土地面积固定，装饰选项少（仅基础路灯、长椅），布局自由度低（“想扩建？只能在巴掌大的地方折腾”）。 - [b]玩法深度不足[/b]：无剧情、无随机事件（如“尸体被盗”），经营仅“埋尸+卖花”，后期缺乏目标（“除了刷天数，不知道该干嘛”）。 - [b]员工AI频繁智障[/b]：花商卡墙、技师无视损坏陷阱、守墓员乱跑，需反复手动重置（“每天花半小时救员工，比打僵尸还累”）。 [h3]2. 基础体验[/h3] - [b]bug频发影响体验[/b]：尸体卡模型消失、炮塔莫名丢失、存档损坏（“第39天存档坏了，13小时进度全没，直接弃坑”）；部分玩家遇游戏崩溃、无法拾取urn。 - [b]操作设计反人类[/b]：除草hitbox诡异（需对准特定角度）、手推车松手bug（前进易自动放手）、菜单字体过小（“老年人得凑到屏幕前看”）。 - [b]防御机制存在缺陷[/b]：木栅栏阻挡炮塔子弹、特斯拉电塔射程短，布局容错率低（“炮塔全打在栅栏上，僵尸无伤拆墓碑”）。 - [b]本地化粗糙[/b]：中文翻译错误多（“培训写成‘火车’，解雇写成‘火’”）、语言选项错位（“选轻松模式，界面仍显普通难度”）。 - [b]存档机制恶心[/b]：仅夜间防御结束后自动存档，中途退出丢失当天进度（“接个电话回来，白天埋的3具尸体全白干”）。 [h3]3. 核心玩法[/h3] - [b]难度两极分化严重[/b]：普通模式前期缺弹药难通关（“夜1僵尸要3枪爆头，弹药不够”），轻松模式后期太简单（“僵尸1枪倒，塔防变观光”），无过渡难度。 - [b]种田系统性价比极低[/b]：农场解锁成本高（3000货币）、土地少、种子贵，回本需20天以上，不如直接买花（“农场是鸡肋，买了用不上”）。 - [b]尸体处理方式单一[/b]：仅支持土葬与火葬，无“定制棺材”“举办葬礼”等个性化服务，浪费“墓园”主题潜力。 - [b]访客互动贫瘠[/b]：访客仅买花或捐赠，无对话、无剧情关联，像“机器人”（“客人买完花就走，毫无互动感”）。 [hr][/hr] [h2]10条玩家希望增加的诉求点（按提及频率降序）[/h2] - [b]增加联机合作模式[/b]：呼吁2-4人联机，支持分工经营（一人种花、一人埋尸）与协作防御（“和朋友守墓打僵尸，能多玩50小时”——对比《i>胡闹厨房》）。 - [b]扩展后期内容[/b]：新增BOSS战、动物僵尸（狗/狼型）、墓园扩建、剧情任务（如“调查僵尸病毒来源”），解决“25天后无目标”问题。 - [b]优化员工AI逻辑[/b]：修复员工卡墙bug，增加任务优先级设置（“让花商只专注卖花，别乱跑修墓碑”）。 - [b]自定义难度选项[/b]：支持调节僵尸数量、血量、经济倍率，满足硬核与休闲玩家需求（“想要‘僵尸多但血薄’的平衡难度”）。 - [b]改进存档机制[/b]：增加手动存档与多存档位，避免“中途退出丢进度”（“打工人需要随时暂停，自动存档太反人类”）。 - [b]重做防御机制[/b]：让栅栏不阻挡子弹、技师自动修墙、延长特斯拉电塔射程，提升防御容错率。 - [b]深化种田与加工系统[/b]：增加作物种类、开放“僵尸尸体→肥料→高级花”加工链，提升农场性价比（“希望种花比买花赚更多”）。 - [b]添加随机事件与剧情[/b]：新增“尸体被盗”“访客闹事”等随机事件，加入主线剧情，丰富体验（“想知道僵尸来源，不只是天天守墓”）。 - [b]优化画质与UI[/b]：增加菜单字体放大、视角防抖开关（部分玩家头晕）、除草视觉提示，提升基础体验。 - [b]扩展武器与道具[/b]：新增近战武器（电锯、斧头）、元素弹药（火焰/电击子弹），提升夜间防御爽感（“想要电锯拆僵尸，铁锹砍太慢”——对比《i>求生之路》）。 [hr][/hr] [h2]玩家提及类似游戏[/h2] https://store.steampowered.com/app/599140/Graveyard_Keeper/ - [b]《墓地管理员（Graveyard Keeper）》[/b]：中世纪墓园经营+暗黑科技，含埋尸、炼金玩法，黑色幽默风格浓郁，适合追求长线模拟的玩家。 https://store.steampowered.com/app/108600/Project_Zomboid/ - [b]《僵尸毁灭工程（Project Zomboid）》[/b]：开放世界硬核生存游戏，支持基地建造与尸潮防御，沙盒自由度高，适合喜欢深度生存体验的玩家。 https://store.steampowered.com/app/1922560/Plants_vs_Zombies_Garden_Warfare_2/ - [b]《植物大战僵尸：花园战争2》[/b]：卡通风格塔防+第三人称射击，支持联机对抗，僵尸设计魔性，适合追求轻松爽感的玩家。

Review: Zombie Graveyard Simulator Developer/Publisher: ThreeW Publisher / Playway S.A. Genre: Simulator / Automation / Survival My Rating: ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ (6/10) **First Impressions** A friend recommended Zombie Graveyard Simulator with heaps of praise. He’s heavy into automation games and that’s exactly the angle he came from. I’m more of a first-person shooter, survival horror, or practical survival type of player, so I went in with a different mindset. For me, it’s okay for a while but not something I’d play all day. About three hours at a time is my limit. **Gameplay** The loop is simple. You dig graves by hand, acquire bodies from jobs via the in-game computer, keep them in cold storage, and bury them. You try to keep the cemetery tidy with flowers and earn money from visitors. Over time, you can hire workers, automate tasks, dabble in farming, and even build up the church. The twist is zombies. Survival mode is on by default but you can toggle it off. With it off, the game quickly becomes repetitive. With it on, you have the nightly challenge of defending your cemetery, building defenses, and putting your money to work. The issue is that survival doesn’t feel mandatory. You can switch it off, stack up money, then turn it back on once you’re ready with turrets and defenses. It would have made more sense if achievements only unlocked with survival left on, but that’s not the case. **Pros** - Chill gameplay, good for casual sessions of three to five hours - Simple automation that unlocks gradually as you hire workers - Developers seem active with updates and community suggestions - Affordable price, good value for what you get **Cons** - Content is shallow so far, most of it can be seen in a day’s play - Zombies feel tacked on rather than fully integrated - Early access means many features are still just on the roadmap (priests, weather system, blood moon events, zombie types, expeditions, research labs) **Comparison** If you’ve played **'Graveyard Keeper'**, this feels like its 3D cousin. Personally, I prefer Graveyard Keeper. It’s polished, fully complete with DLC, and I’d give it a solid 9 out of 10. But if pixel graphics aren’t your style, Zombie Graveyard Simulator offers a similar vibe in a different package, just in its earlier stages. **Final Verdict** I can’t call it amazing, but I wouldn’t dismiss it either. If you enjoy simulators, management systems, and a bit of zombie shooting on the side, it’s worth a try. It’s cheap, it gets updates, and it has room to grow. For me, it’s more of a “play for a few hours now and then” type of game rather than something I’d sink days into. Score: 6/10 Good for fans of quirky simulators, but not essential.

Zombie Graveyard Simulator, developed by threeW and published by PlayWay S.A., is an unusual blend of management simulation and survival action that manages to stand out through its sheer originality. At its core, the game is about running a graveyard, tending to the daily needs of the dead, the mourners, and the grounds themselves. But as night falls, the peaceful cemetery transforms into a battleground, and you’re no longer a caretaker—you’re a survivor. This dichotomy forms the backbone of the gameplay loop, shifting the player between calm, methodical daytime tasks and high-stakes nighttime defense, all within the same cursed patch of earth. By day, players are responsible for maintaining and expanding their graveyard. This isn’t just limited to digging graves and placing headstones. The management elements run surprisingly deep. You tend to the grounds, accept and carry out funeral services, interact with visiting mourners, and handle cremations and burials. Revenue generated can be reinvested into building upgrades, decorations, equipment, and even staff hiring. There’s a surprisingly detailed economy at play, and as your graveyard’s reputation increases, so does the complexity of your responsibilities. You can cultivate flowers, vegetables, and decorative plants to please visitors or boost your resources. Eventually, you gain access to specialized staff like gardeners, florists, technicians, and gravekeepers, each automating or assisting with different parts of your operation. This helps scale the business and frees you up to focus on expansion or preparing for more intense nighttime encounters. But when the sun goes down, the entire atmosphere shifts. The cemetery, once peaceful and businesslike, becomes a target for the undead. At night, the game pivots into a survival-defense mode, where you must fend off waves of zombies trying to escape from the very graves you manage. You’ll construct barricades, repair fences, place traps, and activate turrets. Weapons range from blunt tools like shovels and hammers to firearms and explosives. Combat is tense and fast-paced, requiring you to strategize on the fly—where to station your defenses, how to conserve ammunition, and which threats to prioritize. Zombies escalate in strength and numbers as time progresses, and special variants begin to appear, challenging even the best-prepared gravekeepers. If they breach your defenses, it’s not just your life that’s at risk—the integrity of your graveyard is on the line, and damage done during the night can impact your operations the next day. What makes the game particularly engaging is the way these two modes intertwine. During the day, the money you earn and the improvements you make directly influence your chances of surviving the night. Investing in better security systems, upgrading weapons, or planting light sources to keep zombies at bay becomes crucial. Likewise, the aftermath of each night affects how you plan your day—cleaning up wreckage, repairing structures, and sometimes dealing with the consequences of failed defense. It creates a satisfying loop of preparation, execution, and recovery, with a strong incentive to constantly improve both your facility and your tactics. Visually, the game opts for a slightly stylized aesthetic rather than gritty realism, which works in its favor. The graveyard is detailed and atmospheric, with a soft gothic charm during the day and a creepy, eerie tension at night. The zombies themselves are grotesque enough to be threatening without becoming grotesquely gory, keeping the game accessible while maintaining a horror edge. The UI is functional and fairly easy to navigate, though some menus and systems could benefit from clearer tutorials or tooltips. Environmental details, such as weather effects and lighting, are handled well and help to establish the mood—especially the contrast between the calm sunlit days and the chilling fog of the undead nights. Despite its strengths, Zombie Graveyard Simulator isn’t without its rough spots. The game can feel repetitive in long sessions, especially if you settle into an optimal routine. Visitor requests during the day start to blend together, and while nighttime defense ramps up in difficulty, the patterns eventually become predictable. Some quality-of-life features are underdeveloped; inventory management can feel clunky, staff AI occasionally struggles with prioritization, and there are occasional bugs with zombie pathfinding or trap triggering. Balancing can also feel punishing if you overextend too quickly without the right defenses, leading to frustrating setbacks. However, the developers have been active in updating the game, addressing many of these issues and implementing community feedback, which bodes well for its longevity. Zombie Graveyard Simulator succeeds because it’s more than just a gimmick. What could’ve been a shallow mashup of genres turns into a genuinely compelling hybrid experience, driven by its dual-core gameplay and unusual premise. The contrast between tranquil cemetery operations and desperate zombie defense is not just novel—it’s consistently engaging. It gives players two completely different kinds of challenges that feed into each other in meaningful ways. Whether you’re drawn to the slow satisfaction of building and managing a morbid little empire, or the thrill of holding the line against the dead clawing their way out of the soil, the game offers something distinct. With a few more layers of polish and variety, it could become a standout in both the simulation and survival genres. As it stands, it’s a strange, ambitious, and surprisingly addictive game well worth exploring. Rating: 8/10

Zombie Graveyard Simulator was a really nice surprise when it comes to management games. By day, you are a graveyard keeper...you choose which deceased to accept, prepare their graves based on their wishes then their visitors will arrive to pay their respects, buy flowers from you for the grave and perhaps even attend a church sermon as a form of contemplation. As time goes on and funds start to build via donations, sales and fees for taking on more deceased, you'll then branch into improvements and automation, hiring staff to take care of some of the more mundane work, open up a farm to plant flower seeds so you don't have to buy them, resulting in better profit margins or even opening up a couple of portaloos with a wireless contact card payment meter attached. By night, however...the world becomes more dangerous as...for some reason...you've built your graveyard in a place that's surrounded by the ravenous dead who'll rise and try to eat you, as well as the bodies you've placed in your lovely graves which bolsters their army. To counter this, you will build defences, turrets, barbed wire traps and arm yourself to the teeth to keep the ever growing waves at bay. And, that's the game in a nutshell - I managed to 100% the game in just under 10 hours so it doesn't overstay it's welcome and I could've sunk a couple more making my graveyard look nice and getting the more advanced defences, but I was content to finish where I did....great game! 8/10
